transcript.text: "I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. That's the whole of it."
"What do you remember?"

"It's my grandfather, Lukyan. Went in the Taking. He survived two wars and a famine. Not interesting enough, apparently. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"I'll ask it. I promise."
"You'd do that? Ask it? ...Thank you. Really. Even asking is more than the silence."
"Wait — what were we talking about?"
"Still on that taken person."
"Take your time. I've got nowhere to be."

"A full night's sleep. Just one. Where I don't wake up listening."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid. Good talking."
"Right. Go on, then."
"If it answers -- you'll tell me? Whatever it says. I can take it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Pascaline shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
"Tell me more."
"I'm going hungry — do you have anything to eat? Anything at all? I can't keep going like this."
"Tell me why you need this."
"My stomach's been empty so long I've stopped feeling it, and that's worse. I'm slowing down — stupid, clumsy. Help me get back on my feet."
